title: ADR-0138 D5 ask: on a multi-organisation hosted environment a public form lands in the deployment default organisation — an app serving several legal entities needs the form to name its organisation
body:
Filed from the objectstack-ai/hotsrm design review, 2026-10-23, spec 18.0.0. Related: #23224 (E1 grants channel resolves D4's organisation), #15194 (ADR-0131 epic).

## What the ADR says today
ADR-0138 D4: a public-form submission lands in the deployment's default organisation; a multi-organisation environment is refused until D5 lands. #23224 implemented the D4 resolution.

## The app case
A supplier self-registration form is the front door of an SRM. A group with several legal entities runs one hosted environment with one organisation per entity (ADR-0131 line). Each entity publishes its own registration link; the application must land in that entity's organisation, because admission, approval routes and the supplier number sequence are all organisation-scoped. Under D4 every link lands in the default organisation, and the app cannot move the row afterwards (ADR-0131 D9/D10 forbid re-owning).

The app's current workaround is invited registration only (an organisation invite with the `external` role once #25233 lands), which drops the public link entirely. That is acceptable for v0.2 but not for a public procurement notice (SOE pack) where anyone may apply.

## Wanted (D5 shape, from the app side)
- A public form binds to an organisation at publish time (the form's URL carries the organisation; the grants channel resolves it the way #23224 resolves D4).
- The guest anchor's bindings are evaluated under that organisation; everything else in ADR-0138 unchanged.

## Acceptance
Two organisations in one environment each publish the same package's registration form; a submission on each link lands in its own organisation with its own number sequence; a link for an organisation the form is not published to is refused.

Dedupe words: ADR-0138 D5 public form organisation multi-organisation hosted guest entry per-organisation link.
